D_history_events.event: The Emancipation Proclamation takes effect, declaring freedom for enslaved people in
Ellis Island opens as a U.S. immigration station, receiving millions of newcomers seeking
First U.S. presidential election begins as states appoint electors.
First transatlantic telephone service connects New York and London.
Impeachment trial of President Clinton opens in the U.S. Senate.

The Baltimore and Ohio Railroad is chartered, the first U.S. railroad chartered for commercial passenger and freight service. A steadfast citizen reading this remembers that durable national infrastructure was built by men who bound themselves to long-term work no one was forcing on them — the freely chosen ceiling that holds when the floor wobbles.

The USS Princeton's "Peacemaker" gun explodes during a Potomac River demonstration, killing Secretary of State Abel Upshur, Secretary of the Navy Thomas Gilmer, and six others; President Tyler is below deck and survives. A reminder that even the strongest engines of state can fail catastrophically when men trust the metal more than the LORD — and that a steadfast citizen treats every public office, every public moment, as held in lent hands.
